description:
FILED s531a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-01) from #1705 acceptance (Pod-Simple JustPod_corpus.t runs since %Config lists Encode).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3):
  use Encode;
  for my $e (qw(big5 big5-eten koi8-r iso-2022-jp cp1256 iso-8859-11)) { my $o = Encode::find_encoding($e); print "$e=", ($o ? $o->name : "none"), "/", Encode::resolve_alias($e) || "noalias", " " }
perl: big5=big5-eten/big5-eten big5-eten=big5-eten/big5-eten koi8-r=koi8-r/koi8-r iso-2022-jp=iso-2022-jp/iso-2022-jp cp1256=cp1256/cp1256 iso-8859-11=iso-8859-11/iso-8859-11
PCL:  big5=none/big5-eten big5-eten=none/big5-eten koi8-r=koi8-r/koi8-r iso-2022-jp=none/iso-2022-jp ...

Two faces of one gap: the CJK tables (Encode::TW big5-eten, Encode::JP iso-2022-jp) are not in lib/Encode.pm, and resolve_alias still answers their canonical names, so a caller that checks resolve_alias first (Pod::Simple::TranscodeSmart::encoding_is_available) then gets undef from find_encoding and dies.  At least make the two agree (rule 12: an encoding PCL cannot decode must not be advertised); the tables themselves are a shim feature (lib/Encode.pm, rule 9a).  Board: Pod-Simple JustPod_corpus.t *PLAN* (ran 1 of 19; row 1 is #1389), blessed to this task by s531a.  Probe: s531a scratch/s531a/pr/enc2.pl.

=== DONE IN CODE (s539a), board rows NOT YET CLOSED ===
MEASURED first (scratch/s539a/m5/enc1.pl in the s539a worktree: perl's `Encode->encodings(":all")` = 124 names + 18 common aliases, resolve_alias and find_encoding under perl vs PCL): PCL answered perl's name through resolve_alias and undef through find_encoding for 18 (big5 / big5-eten / big5-hkscs / cp949 / cp950 / euc-cn / gb2312 / euc-kr / hz / johab / iso-2022-jp / -kr / 7bit-jis / cp932); 57 more were undef in both (SBCL has no codec, and PCL never advertised them).  SBCL's external formats (sb-int:get-external-format over the list): cp932 YES -- WIRED in lib/Encode.pm (%INFO + the aliases windows-31j / ms932 / x-sjis; cp-932 / windows-932 through the cp regex); its whole double-byte repertoire matches perl's (11,471 sequences: 9,795 decodable, the same checksum, the same 398 one-way pairs).  The rest are no longer advertised: resolve_alias answers undef when no codec exists (%NOCODEC deleted) -- both lookups agree (rule 12).  The missing tables, sized, are #4885.  not-supported "Encode: encodings with no codec" and DECIDED (## s513i line marked SUPERSEDED, ## s539a) updated.  Guard Pl/t/encode-shim-01.t block 5 (rows 87-108; 87-100 106-108 fail on the base).
BOARD: Pod-Simple JustPod_corpus.t 0/1 of 19 rc 255 -> 18/1 of 19 rc 1 (the big5 POD now passes; row 1 = 8859_7.pod, #1389, stays); its *PLAN* row LEFT the baseline by edit.
OWED (CLOSE-WITH-ROWS): Pod-Simple corpus.t carries 14 rows keyed #4167 (the 2202jp*.txt / laozi38 files: "WHAT ENCODING!?!?"); their one-file run base -> tree was queued and cancelled at the s541 stop (scratch/s539a/legs/board2.sh, not taken).  Do not close #4167 before those rows are re-read.
subject: Encode shim: resolve_alias names big5 / big5-eten / iso-2022-jp but find_encoding answers undef for them -- Pod::Simple::TranscodeSmart dies "WHAT ENCODING!?!?" on a big5 POD
